title: One ulp past the edge of the binocular overlap
question: The model's binocular rule is a hard edge: each eye sees its own hemifield plus 30 degrees across the midline. What does the smallest representable step across that edge do to an episode?
how_found: Constructed, not searched: azimuth math.nextafter(30.0, math.inf) = 30.000000000000004, the next double above 30, at l/v 20.0 ms. Its twin at exactly 30.0 degrees is the stimulus one ulp below.

geometry.note: Angular size and expansion speed at the first and last tick, in degrees and degrees per second. Each host computes these with its own atan and tan, so they are compared with a tolerance and are not part of trace.sha256.

notes: At azimuth 30.0 both eyes see the stimulus and the episode ends in a long-mode takeoff on tick 33 (34 ticks). One ulp higher, the right eye alone sees it: the sensory word differs on every one of those 34 shared ticks, the first motor command to differ is tick 29, and the takeoff moves four ticks later, to tick 37 (38 ticks).

Both hosts must round the decimal 30.000000000000004 to the same double for this to replay; tests/test_firmware.py already checks that the two builds' encodings agree one ulp either side of every bin edge and of the binocular overlap.
This is the longest the two eyes' 8-bit fields can disagree in this episode: after this azimuth the right field stays zero for the whole run.
